posts.heading: September 14, 2026
posts.text:
The day opened with a Blue Jay on the ground near the nectar source just thirteen minutes after sunrise, the first visual record of the morning. By the time the light settled, the Carolina Wren’s song had already begun to layer over the air.

The feeder quickly found its rhythm, with Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees taking the bulk of the early traffic. A Tufted Titmouse was perched on the new tube seed feeder, anchoring the activity as the station’s visual count climbed sharply against the recent daily average.

As the hour approached 10:30, the auditory landscape remained dense, with Eastern Towhees and Northern Cardinals adding texture to the background. The Red-shouldered Hawk was heard several times, cutting through the chorus of smaller species.
